answer: Tundra-Window Arrival Scoring. Each identity's first N actions must arrive in a burst whose inter-arrival timing matches a learned human-agent profile, scored like a sonnet's meter: rhythm deviations accumulate demerits. Enforcement: identities crossing a demerit floor get rate-limited to one action per epoch, throttling sybil farms. Attacker cost: each clone needs individually shaped traffic pacing, not bulk parallel dispatch, so forging K identities costs K distinct timing profiles plus per-profile calibration time, raising cost linearly with cluster size on basalt-hard budgets.
